chunks: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Walid al-Salmy narrated to us, saying: Abulfazl Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Katib al-Neishaboory narrated through his chain, elevating it to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), that he said:

A man’s perfection lies in six characteristics: two minor ones, two major ones, and two influential ones. As for the two minor ones, they are his heart and his tongue; if he fights, he fights with conviction (inner strength), and if he speaks, he speaks with eloquence. As for the two major ones, they are his intellect and his aspiration/determination. As for the two influential ones, they are his wealth and his beauty.
ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics that define a man's perfection according to Imam Ali in al-Khisal?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a holistic framework for human perfection, balancing internal spiritual integrity with external social presence. The classification into 'minor' (inner faculties), 'major' (cognitive and volitional), and 'influential' (external markers) reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of character and conduct. This teaching underscores that true nobility arises not merely from status, but from the alignment of one’s heart, speech, intellect, and ambition with divine guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-43 Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Walid al-Salmy narrated that Abulfazl Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Katib al-Neishaboory quoted through documents linking up to the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) saying,

“A man’s perfection lies in six characteristics: two minor ones, two major ones, and two influential ones. And the two minor ones lie in his heart and tongue in that he fights with his heart, and he expresses his words with his tongue. And the two major ones lie in his intellect and determination. And the two influential ones lie in his wealth and beauty.”
